title: Concept-Formation and Measurement-Omission
summary: Differentiation, integration, and concepts as a mathematical process of measurement-omission.

lessons.title: Set the group apart
lessons.objective: Isolate units by what they share with each other and how they differ from a wider background.

exercises.prompt: What is the first move in forming a concept?

choices.text: Isolate a group from a wider background
Write a dictionary definition first
Invent a word with no observed group
Wait until the items feel alike

feedback.note: Concept-formation starts by setting some existents apart from the rest of what you perceive.

exercises.prompt: A similarity you can use for a concept holds between how many existents?

choices.text: At least two
Exactly one, with nothing to compare
None; likeness is supplied by the word
Only when every existent in the world is included

feedback.note: Differentiation needs more than one unit. A lone item has no similar members to group.

exercises.prompt: Match each move to what it does in differentiation.

pairs.right: See what the members have in common
See how the group differs from the background
Treat the similar existents as one group

feedback.note: You differentiate by likeness inside the group and difference from what you leave outside it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the two sides of differentiation.

feedback.note: Both sides are required. Similarity without a contrast does not mark a group off from the rest.

exercises.prompt: Put the first step in order.

feedback.note: Differentiation works on what you already perceive. It does not invent the units.

exercises.prompt: In this process, a unit is an existent regarded as what?

choices.text: A separate member of a group
A dictionary entry
A private mood
A replacement for the axioms

feedback.note: A unit is one existent looked at as a member of the group you are isolating.

exercises.prompt: Match each mistake to the differentiation rule it breaks.

pairs.left: Grouping a single item with no peers
Ignoring how the group differs from the rest
Sorting by what you wish were true

feedback.note: The group is carved from perception by real likeness and real contrast, not by a wish.

exercises.prompt: Name the background the group is set against.

parts.text: The units are isolated from a

feedback.note: The background is the wider field of existents you are not putting in this group.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states what differentiation produces.

feedback.note: The product of this step is an isolated group, not yet the integrated concept.

lessons.title: Unite the units
lessons.objective: Integrate the isolated units into one new mental entity, the concept.

exercises.prompt: After the units are isolated, what does integration do with them?

choices.text: Unites them into one mental entity
Drops them and keeps only a word
Splits each unit into sensations
Lets a group vote them into one thing

feedback.note: Integration is the uniting step. The many units become one concept in your mind.

exercises.prompt: What kind of entity is a concept?

choices.text: A mental integration of units
A physical object sitting beside the units
An emotion about the units
A statute passed about the units

feedback.note: The concept is not a new physical object. It is the mental product of integrating the units.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its role.

feedback.note: Differentiation isolates. Integration then treats those units as one concept.

exercises.prompt: Complete the description of a concept.

feedback.note: Two or more units are required. One item alone is not an integration.

exercises.prompt: Order the two main acts of concept-formation so far.

feedback.note: You isolate the group first, then unite its members into the concept.

exercises.prompt: Why call the concept a new mental entity?

choices.text: Many units are now held as one
A new physical existent has been created
You now know less than the percepts showed
The feeling replaces the units

feedback.note: The newness is mental. The units stay what they are; your mind now holds them as one.

exercises.prompt: Match the count to the right description.

pairs.right: Not enough to form a concept

feedback.note: Integration reduces many observed units to one mental entity. Zero units leaves nothing to unite.

exercises.prompt: Fill the verb that names this step.

feedback.note: The name of the uniting step is integration.

exercises.prompt: Build the result of a successful integration.

feedback.note: Success means one concept, not a new physical thing and not a feeling standing in for the units.

exercises.prompt: Does integration throw away the fact that the members are distinct existents?

choices.text: No. It holds distinct units as one mental group
Yes. The members stop being separate existents
Only if a committee agrees
Yes. It replaces them with raw sensations

feedback.note: The units remain distinct existents. The concept is how your mind holds them together.

lessons.title: Same characteristic, different measure
lessons.objective: Treat similarity as the same characteristic possessed in different measure, so the process is mathematical.

exercises.prompt: On this account, two units are similar when they share what?

choices.text: The same characteristic in different measure
The same nickname and nothing else
The same feeling in the observer
No characteristic at all

feedback.note: Similarity here is not a vague likeness. It is one characteristic appearing in more than one measurement.

exercises.prompt: Why is concept-formation called a mathematical process?

choices.text: The shared characteristic comes in measurements
You must solve an equation before you may look
Only numbers can be conceptualized
A majority assigns the quantities

feedback.note: The mathematics is the measurements of a characteristic, not a requirement that every concept be a numeral.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to its place in the measurement story.

pairs.right: What the units have in common
The amount or degree of that characteristic

feedback.note: Keep the characteristic distinct from the particular amount in which a given unit has it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the formula for similarity.

feedback.note: If the measure did not differ, you would not be relating distinct units by degree.

exercises.prompt: Build the mathematical claim in plain order.

feedback.note: A characteristic relevant to a concept is present in some quantity. A measure of none is not that characteristic.

exercises.prompt: Must every unit in the group have the same numerical amount?

choices.text: No. The amounts may differ
Yes. Only identical amounts can be grouped
Yes. The amount must be zero
The characteristic need not be measurable

feedback.note: The group is held together by the characteristic, while the particular measurements are allowed to vary.

exercises.prompt: Match the example pattern to the idea it illustrates.

pairs.left: A darker red and a lighter red

feedback.note: Length and shade are characteristics that come in degree. A label by itself is not a measurement.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two words that make the process mathematical.

feedback.note: Mathematical here means measurement of a characteristic, not a mood and not an arbitrary tag.

exercises.prompt: State what may vary inside one group.

feedback.note: Variation belongs to the measurements. The characteristic those measurements are of stays the basis of the group.

lessons.title: Omit the particular measurements
lessons.objective: Form the concept by retaining the characteristic and omitting the particular measurements.

exercises.prompt: When the concept is formed, which measurements are omitted?

choices.text: The particular measurements of the units
The characteristic itself
The fact that any measurement exists
The percepts that supplied the evidence

feedback.note: Measurement-omission drops the specific amounts. It does not drop the characteristic or the evidence.

exercises.prompt: What does the concept retain?

choices.text: The characteristic, without the specific amounts
Only the measurement of the first unit you saw
Neither the characteristic nor any awareness of measure
Whatever amount you prefer

feedback.note: You keep the attribute and let the specific quantities go. The concept is not tied to one specimen’s amount.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to whether the concept keeps it.

pairs.left: The requirement that some measurement exists

feedback.note: Omitting the particulars is not denying that the characteristic has some measurement on each unit.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rule of measurement-omission.

feedback.note: That pair of actions is measurement-omission: keep the kind of attribute, drop the specific measures.

exercises.prompt: Build what the concept covers.

feedback.note: Because the specific amounts are omitted, the concept is open to the measurements you have not met yet.

exercises.prompt: A new table is longer than any table you have seen. Does the concept still cover it?

choices.text: Yes. Its length is another measurement of the same characteristic
No. Concepts freeze the first measurements you noticed
Only after a poll adds it
Only if it feels like a table

feedback.note: Omission makes the concept open-ended across the range of measurements, including ones not yet observed.

exercises.prompt: Match each error to what it confuses.

pairs.left: Dropping the characteristic along with the amounts
Locking the concept to one specimen’s size
Saying the units have no measurement at all

feedback.note: The omitted item is the particular measurement, not the characteristic and not the fact of quantity.

exercises.prompt: Fill the word for the range the concept leaves open.

parts.text: With the particulars omitted, the concept is

feedback.note: Open-ended means later measurements of the same characteristic still fall under the concept.

exercises.prompt: State the omission in one line.

feedback.note: Say what is omitted and what is not. The characteristic stays; the specific measures do not.

lessons.title: One mathematical process
lessons.objective: Run differentiation, integration, and measurement-omission as one ordered process that yields a concept.

exercises.prompt: Which order is the process?

choices.text: Differentiate, integrate, omit the particular measurements
Omit measurements before you have any units
Choose a word, then look for something it might fit
Feel a likeness, then skip the characteristic

feedback.note: The acts are one process in that order: isolate, unite, and omit the specific measures.

exercises.prompt: What does the full process produce?

choices.text: A concept: units integrated with measurements omitted
A new sense organ
A substitute for existence and identity
An emotion used as evidence

feedback.note: The product is a concept. It is not a new faculty of sense and not a feeling standing in for knowledge.

exercises.prompt: Match each stage to its job.

pairs.right: Unite them into one mental entity
Drop the particular amounts, keep the characteristic

feedback.note: Each stage has one job. Together they are concept-formation.

exercises.prompt: Name the process in the unit’s own terms.

parts.text: A concept is formed by differentiation,

feedback.note: Those three names are the whole of this unit: differentiate, integrate, omit measurements.

exercises.prompt: Build the process from start to product.

tokens.text: replace the units with a wish

feedback.note: Follow the units from a perceived group to one concept whose specific measures are omitted.

exercises.prompt: Where do the units in this process come from?

choices.text: From perceived existents
From words that exist before any awareness
From dreams that need no evidence
From a vote about what should exist

feedback.note: Concept-formation works on existents you perceive. It does not start from a free-floating word.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the verdict.

pairs.left: One object, no contrast, no integration
A feeling with no measured characteristic

feedback.note: Use the full process as the test. A lone item or a bare feeling has not completed it.

exercises.prompt: Fill the kind of process the unit assigns to concepts.

feedback.note: The unit’s name for the process is mathematical because it omits measurements of a characteristic.

exercises.prompt: Close the unit in one sentence.

feedback.note: That is the unit in one line: integration of units through measurement-omission.

exercises.prompt: Which question belongs to this unit rather than a later one?

choices.text: How are units integrated by omitting measurements?
How should a definition be worded as a later step?
What is the proper role of government?
What makes a painting romanticist?

feedback.note: This unit stops at the mathematical process itself: differentiation, integration, and measurement-omission.
